 Historic first for New Zealand batter following India century
 Glenn Phillips has become the first player to score centuries across all formats against India in the same calendar year.
 19 November, 2026 New Zealand batter Glenn Phillips created history on Friday when he became the first player in the history of the game to have scored a century against India across all three formats in the same calendar year.
 Phillips completed the feat courtesy of his superb innings of 118 against India in the first ICC World Test Championship contest in Wellington, adding to previous hundreds against the Asian side in ODI and T20I fixtures already in 2026.

 It is just the second time in history that the feat has been completed, with Phillips joining Rohit Sharma as the only previous player to have scored centuries against the same opposition across all formats in the same calendar year after the India great did so against Sri Lanka at the backend of 2017.
 Phillips' second Test century helped New Zealand push their first innings today out beyond 300 early on the second day at Basin Reserve , with the right-hander combining well with Henry Nicholls for a partnership of 216 as the hosts recovered from a precarious position of 70/5 midway through the opening day.

 Akash Deep finally ended Phillips' resistance when he got one to move away and take the top of off stump, with Nicholls remaining unmoved as he continues to build a big innings after he scored his 12th Test century on the opening day.
 New Zealand will be hoping to build their advantage as they look to make a push for next year's World Test Championship Final at The Oval, with the side currently sitting in second place on the standings and just two spots ahead of India.
